newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard says not seeking early Australian poll.
newsitem.headline: Howard says not seeking early Australian poll.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he was not seeking an early election to force the upper house of parliament, the Senate, to pass his legislative programme.
Such an election, a double dissolution, was always an option, Howard told Melbourne radio 3AW. "But it's not something that I seek," he said.
Analysts have speculated Howard's government, elected in March for a three-year term, could be forced to call an early election to implement key reforms.

The government is struggling to win parliamentary approval for its planned sale of one-third of state telecoms company Telstra Corp. It needs the support of at least two non-government senators in the upper house Senate, where it does not have a majority.
Australia's constitution allows both houses of parliament to be dissolved and a fresh election called if the Senate rejects legislation twice within three months.
A joint sitting of both houses can then be called to consider contentious legislation.

The planned partial privatisation of Telstra would raise an estimated A$8 billion -- A$1 billion of which would be used to create a special fund for environment spending and the remainder would be used to repay government debt.
